scenarios.8: Sens: COD delay 6 months, no LDs
scenarios.11: Sens: SEKA pays 120 days late for 12 months

P-F02.index_reading_month: 2021-09 (three-month lag; September reading for the January reset)
P-F02.fx_note: model uses the 2022H1 average rate (654.9) as the invoice-date rate
P-F02.capacity_note: reset to the tested 581.9 MW at taking-over (November 2021), before the first invoice

P-F32.note: Illustrative monthly invoice built with the model formulas for one month (the model itself is semiannual)

P-F03.note: A-loan and B-loan upfront fees not given for 2016; close-level fees used (1.25%, 1.50%)

P-F04.basis: IFRS, USD functional currency; plant as property, plant and equipment depreciated straight line over the 25-year PPA term to nil at transfer; SEKA receivables at amortized cost (no ECL provision modeled)

P-F05.note: Debt set at each gearing level and sculpted to FC base CFADS (constant DSCR); DSCR and downside tests not applied

P-F06.basis: 25 years at 10.0% (flat real flows, so the discount rate cancels), 70% dispatch at 588.4 MW, gas USD 5.50/MMBtu, contracted heat rate 6,323 kJ/kWh, 2016 prices, capacity paid in full

definitions.dscr: CFADS / (interest + swap net + PRI premium + scheduled principal) in the period
definitions.avg_dscr: debt-service-weighted: sum CFADS / sum debt service over the loan life
definitions.llcr: (PV of CFADS to final maturity at the period all-in senior cost + DSRA balance) / senior debt outstanding, at the start of the first repayment period
definitions.gearing: senior debt / total funding requirement (all uses incl. IDC, fees, ECA premium and DSRA)

P-F09.eca_rules: OECD Arrangement project finance terms for 2018 commitments (t-oecd-pf-2018; annex 3.6): repayment term <= 14 years; first repayment <= 24 months after COD with at least 2% repaid by then; WAL <= 7.25 years; <= 25% of principal in any six months

P-F10.cfads_definition: revenue - operating costs - tax paid - increase in working capital - MMRA contributions + MMRA releases; MMRA inside; DSRA flows and DSRA interest excluded (nil); DSU and BI proceeds included when received; performance LDs excluded (they prepay debt); late payment interest received included

P-F14.note: OY values allocate each semiannual period by its operating months (OY1 = May 2021 to April 2022)

P-F15.payment_order: SHL interest, SHL principal, dividends within distributable reserves; remainder trapped

P-F16.breakeven_basis: FC base debt locked; breakeven = minimum period DSCR of 1.00x; months covered = (DSRA + LC) / monthly outflows in 2022H1
P-F16.equity_irr_basis: project-company level, from the LNTP date (2018-02-05), before shareholder withholding tax
P-F16.debt_capacity_basis: Debt F130: PV at the sculpting rate of the scenario's CFADS from the first repayment to June 30, 2034, divided by 1.35, with the contract profile and amount (debt locked); the FC base value equals the senior debt (DSCR binding)

P-F17.note: Each error alone, re-sized with the sizing loop (DSCR, gearing and downside constraints); downside run with the erroneous model locked at its own sizing

E1.description: Capacity payment without the availability cap (A/90% not capped at 1)

E2.description: LTSA variable fee on one gas turbine instead of two

E3.description: Tariff indexation reads the index at period end instead of the lagged (Sep/Mar) reading

E4.description: Senior loan interest on 30/360 instead of ACT/360

E5.description: Full tax exemption applied to OY1-OY8 (15% band ignored)

E6.description: Deferred holiday depreciation lost (pool never credited)

E7.description: DSRA initial funding drawn 100% from senior debt instead of pro rata

E9.description: Fuel-charge revenue uses a typed 76.5% dispatch instead of the live dispatch

E10.description: Swap net settlement with legs reversed

annual_shadow_sizing.basis: calendar-year CFADS from the first repayment period (2021H2) to June 30, 2034; each year discounted at its year end at the FC base sculpting rates compounded within the year; 1.35x; the difference against the semiannual sizing is the time-grain effect

epc_claims.name: EPC claims settlement: COVID-19 disruption and compensable events beyond the 9.40 variation order (Lindauer, settled at taking-over)

acceleration.name: Acceleration agreement with Lindauer to hold taking-over at November 2021 after the grid event

owner_site.name: Extended owner's costs and site team beyond the 6.93 (owner's engineer, site team, security, camp)

recommissioning.name: Re-commissioning after the grid event (repeat backfeed, protection coordination study, OEM field service)

transformer.name: Transformer replacement expediting, freight and installation not recovered under the EAR policy

ie_legal.name: Additional IE, lenders' legal and expert-determination costs beyond the 0.86

operator.name: Operator mobilization and training held seven months longer (O&M contractor standby)

P-F18.finding: After the unused contingency, delay LDs, DSU proceeds and the KCR depreciation on the onshore EPC, the remaining overrun was funded 75:25 by the standby facility and contingent equity (delay-related costs by category, P-C43)

P-F22.hedged_note: the swap floating leg is modeled equal to the loan base rate, so the spread adjustment cancels on the hedged portion; the H1 2023 LIBOR/SOFR basis is ignored

P-F23.interest_limitation: grandfathered: bond principal only refinances the prepaid principal plus costs (no upsizing)

P-F24.basis: equity value = PV of projected shareholder distributions (SHL interest, SHL principal, dividends) from the actual-history run after the locked-box date; price includes shares and shareholder loans pro rata

P-F26.basis: IFRS 10 loss of control: gain = consideration + fair value of the retained 36% (price per point x 36) - 60% of (book equity + shareholder loans) at completion, IFRS basis per P-F56 (pre-tax adjustment); the parent share of the hedge reserve (swap MTM at 3.40%) is recycled to profit; balances interpolated to September 30, 2026

P-F27.note: Treaty rates apply to Kilnworth (treaty holding company); totals are for 100% of shareholders over the PPA life; gross-up cost = 10% WHT borne on grossed-up commercial and standby (commercial share) interest incl. construction

P-F29.plant_condition: assumption-based: handback works equal to the accumulated reserve at expiry (USD 1 transfer)

P-F33.basis: FC base, 2021H2 (first full period after scheduled COD), per calendar day

P-F35.note: FC downside uses base dispatch 76.5% (Case Bible 1.10 definition)

P-F37.note: refund-lag cost = interest on the UBK VAT facility (policy rate + 2.50%)

P-F38.rule: Shareholder loans count as related-party debt; equity = share capital + positive retained earnings; deductible share = min(1, 3 x equity / SHL balance at period start)
P-F38.tax_effect_note: during the holiday and while deferred depreciation shelters income the disallowance has little or no cash-tax effect

P-F39.rule: annex 1.1.5: capacity charges at 100% on contracted capacity; energy charges at contracted capacity x 730 h x 90% x 76.5% dispatch plan; that period's indices and gas price

P-F40.netting_basis: set-offs under the June 29, 2023 agreement equal the fall in energy-charge arrears matched by deferred SNHK/GCK payables, spread evenly over the six months of each half-year (the model is semiannual); cap USD 9.0m a month

inputs.availability_shock: per operating year, normal(0, 2.0 points), truncated to -10/+5 points, independent across years
inputs.heat_rate_degradation: non-recoverable rate per year, normal(0.12%, 0.04%), floored at 0
inputs.fx: KCR depreciation drift per year, normal(5.19%, 3.0%) applied to the FC FX path
inputs.debt: locked at the FC base contract (amount and repayment profile)

equity_first.note: Equity drawn first, then debt; gearing 75% of the resulting total funding requirement; swap notional assumed to accrete at 80% of drawn debt; DSCR test not applied (illustrative variant).

P-F36.note: Sized on DSCR target and gearing cap only (downside shown as a test)

P-F47.note: FC base; contracted 6,323 kJ/kWh (+0.10%/yr) vs plant 6,261 x (1+0.12%/yr) x 1.008 recoverable; both x 1.023 part load; the margin turns negative when plant degradation overtakes the allowance

P-F48.note: EOH = 8,059 hours x dispatch/76.5 + 38 starts x 10; the actual run-out uses base dispatch after 2022 (2022 drought adds about 8% to that year)

P-F49.note: Development cost reimbursement split per annex 1.14.1: Phase 1 USD 1.5 million Kilnworth, remainder 70:30 with Talme in-kind credit included; the ABDB fund premium is paid by the fund to the selling sponsors, outside the project company

P-F51.rule: 1.15% a year on 90% of the commercial balance; model accrues with each period (annex: semiannually in advance); cancelled 2025-06-30

P-F53.ecl_note: ages each half-year increase as half 1-90 days and half 91-180 days at its period end, older layers over 180 days; reductions first-in first-out
P-F53.hedge_reserve_note: cash flow hedge assumed fully effective: hedge reserve = swap MTM (before deferred tax); at close the MTM is the negative value of the 7.5 bps charge

P-F56.note: Financial asset at cost at COD = capitalized cost on the lenders basis; receivable stream = capital charge component at 100% availability on 581.9 MW; EIR fixed at COD (semiannual, stream at period end, no finance income in the COD period); IFRIC 12 profit before tax = lenders basis + finance income - capital charge collected + depreciation; deferred tax not remeasured

P-F54.label: estimate; simplified basis per input request 43; 2026 to September 30 at 60% (consolidated period)

P-F55.note: annual RAROC on loan holds (swap line not risk-weighted: exposure measure not specified); slotting construction 115%, operations 90%; ECA-covered 95% at 0%; PRI not recognized; 13.5% capital; funding premium 0.45%; opex 0.15%; tax 19%; hurdle 12%

P-F57.note: 2015 USD, 10% discount rate, flat costs; HHV/LHV 1.108 for gas

P-F58.note: comparison at 76.5% uses the COD re-forecast run (same plant and COD, FC-style macro after 2021)

P-F59.note: Illustrative. Logic corrected in v1.2: production equals gas sold to SNHK (capped at contracted demand of about 106 MMscfd, not the 150 MMscfd plateau capacity) and cash flows run to a 40% reserve tail; development capex is funded by the facility and equity and excluded from the borrowing-base NPV (completion basis). With the annex inputs the 2023 base lands near 360; signing comes out lower than 2023 because cash flows start two years later and the 2017 Brent deck is lower, so a signing base of about 420 would need a gas price near the value shown (kept for reference); the annex expectation was revised to the model values in v1.3 (P-C46)

P-F60.note: annuity shortcut on capacity and fixed O&M revenue less fixed costs (energy margin ignored), 13 years at the 2016 indicative weighted all-in cost (P-F03)

P-F62.note: bid-model IRRs are Kilnworth 2016 bid-model inputs (annex 4.7), not reference-model outputs

P-F63.prepayment_basis: eq:51.3: (DS - CFADS/level) / (P/D + i), prepayment applied pro rata and deemed made at the start of the test period (July 1, 2022); P = scheduled principal in the 12 months, D = senior debt at the start, i = all-in senior rate a year at the start of the test (2 x the 2022H2 period rate, Ratios row 7). Proportional version (eq:37.4): (DS - CFADS/level) x D / DS

P-F65.instrument: USD/KCR forwards buying KCR, cash-settled in USD (non-deliverable)
P-F65.pricing: covered interest parity: 519.4 x ((1 + 13.5%) / (1 + FC forward 6M LIBOR))^(years to settlement)
P-F65.vat_note: The KCR VAT facility is not hedged: it is matched by the KCR VAT refund receivable (natural hedge); only the facility interest is exposed

P-F66.finding: The forwards locked in forward points of roughly 10% a year (KCR policy rate against USD LIBOR) while the cauri fell about 5% a year to 2021, so the project gained on the hedge; the hedge does not transfer the depreciation benefit to the bank. Settlements reduce the construction uses before the standby facility is drawn.

steps.step: Kilnworth bid model, September 2016 (reconstructed; tariff USD 14.36/kW-month)
Base rate: reconstructed bid-model swapped rate (flat) replaced by the FC forward curve and the 2.947% swap
Debt terms: 2016 indicative margins, upfront fees and ECA premium (annex 4.7) replaced by the FC terms
PRI cover on the commercial tranche and the 10% WHT gross-up, added in diligence
Soft mini-perm cash sweep from 2027 (FC term sheet)
Capex: bid-stage USD 655.0m before financing grows to the FC budget of USD 710.99m (owner's cost, resettlement, contingency)
VAT facility interest (omitted from the bid model, annex Kunal Mehrotra)
Tax: minimum turnover tax and thin-cap disallowance
FX: KCR depreciation on the local tariff shares and costs (bid model held the KCR flat)
IRR dating: measured from the February 2018 LNTP payment rather than from financial close

P-F64.note: Sequential attribution from the reconstructed bid model to the FC base, in the order shown; each step re-sizes debt (DSCR 1.35x, 75% gearing cap, downside 1.20x). Steps sum exactly to the gap (no residual). The one undocumented bid input, the swapped base rate, is solved at 3.44% flat so that the reconstruction returns 16.0%; it is a modeler reconstruction, read as a conservative bid-stage rate (2016 USD swap rates were about 1.5% to 2.0%). Reordering the steps changes individual steps, never the total.
